subject: Sealed-site bootstrap + emergency image swap (validation & handoff)
messages:
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@acmepharm.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T08:21:00+00:00
Subject: Request: sealed-site bootstrap and emergency swap process

Hi Aditya / Laura,

We're preparing for our compliance review around our planned sealed (air-gapped) deployment of Redwood Private. The auditor wants a clear, step-by-step runbook for the initial bootstrap (first install from physical media) and an emergency image-swap procedure in case a signed image fails validation in the field.

Can you provide:
- A concise checklist we can attach to the audit package describing media handoff, signature verification, and operator validation steps.
- A fallback procedure for replacing the image on an islanded cluster with minimal downtime and auditable manifest updates.
- Any requirements we should communicate to our on-site operators (keys, HSM presence, USB/CD verification steps).

Time is tight—auditor review is scheduled for the week of Jan 10. If possible, we'd like a short dry-run prior to that.

Thanks,
Jake
Infra Lead, Acme Pharmaceuticals
[Attachment: none]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-07T11:15:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Request: sealed-site bootstrap and emergency swap process

Jake — thanks for the clear ask. Draft attached (sealed-bootstrap-checklist.pdf) plus a concise emergency playbook (emergency-swap-playbook.md). High-level approach below; please confirm gaps you need filled for the auditor.

Proposed sealed-site bootstrap (high-level):
1) Pre-ship: Build signed image bundles on our build cluster. Each bundle gets: image.tar.gz, signed-manifest.csv, and a timestamped signature from Redwood's release HSM.
2) Transfer: Physical transfer (air-gapped media) with chain-of-custody manifest populated and dual-operator initials at pickup/dropoff.
3) On-site verification: Operator computes local checksum, validates manifest signature against Redwood release key (public cert included in bundle), and verifies timestamp.
4) Offline validation: Operator boots a validation node in isolated mode; runs smoke tests (health probes, KV-store integrity) included in the checklist.
5) Acceptance: Operator signs acceptance line on manifest and uploads (secure courier) or seals and sends scanned manifest per your compliance process.

Emergency image-swap (fast fallback):
- Trigger condition: primary image fails startup validation or post-boot integrity tests.
- Precondition: site must have a pre-provisioned fallback image (kept on separate sealed media) and a signed rollback manifest.
- Steps: 1) Quiesce traffic; 2) Perform an offline signature verification of fallback image; 3) Replace image on control plane host(s) following exact block-device write commands in playbook; 4) Run smoke test suite; 5) Append swap record to manifest and capture operator signatures + time.

Key notes / suggestions for your operators:
- HSM: If your site has an HSM, use it for local timestamping; otherwise require dual external sign-off.
- Dual-signature: For any emergency swap, require two operators to sign the manifest (operator + security lead).
- Validation window: Plan a 10–15 minute maintenance window for the swap; include rollback instructions if swap fails.

Ask: can we schedule a 90-minute dry-run with your infra team the week of Jan 3? We'll walk through the checklist and run the smoke tests inside a sealed staging room.

Attachments included: sealed-bootstrap-checklist.pdf, emergency-swap-playbook.md (staged drafts).

—
Aditya Rao
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-08T09:02:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Request: sealed-site bootstrap and emergency swap process

Thanks Aditya — solid draft. A couple of compliance-driven edits we should include before sending to the auditor: 

1) Dual-release signatures: Require two independent Redwood release keys (primary + quorum key) on production image bundles for any customer in regulated industries. Not just a dual operator on-site; the artifact itself must carry two signatures.

2) Timestamping and TSA: Include an authoritative timestamp (TSP) on the signed manifest (not just HSM local time) so auditor can verify non-repudiation. We should incorporate a TSA reference field into the manifest template (see attached signed-manifest-template.csv).

3) Manifest contents: Add fields for operator badge ID, transport carrier (if couriered), and geo-location (site ID). Auditors expect these in the chain-of-custody.

4) Emergency test acceptance criteria: Define precise smoke test pass thresholds (e.g., 200ms median p50 latency on inference endpoint, KV-read consistency, and successful load of model weights into KV). If failure occurs, automatic reimage path should kick in after 6 minutes with clear logs captured.

Karthik — please confirm that the emergency-swap-playbook.md uses our standard device write commands and preserves device serial mapping (critical to avoid re-partition mistakes).

Jake — if you want, we'll update the attached drafts and re-send a consolidated PDF for your auditor. We should also lock in the Jan 5 dry-run call mentioned below — Jan 3 works for our team but Jan 5 gives your infra team more time. Which do you prefer?

Laura
Dir, Platform Security, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: signed-manifest-template.csv (CSV, 3KB)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Jake / team — thanks everyone for the input. Confirming next steps from Redwood: 

1) We'll produce a consolidated audit packet (single PDF) that includes: the sealed-bootstrap-checklist, the emergency-swap-playbook with explicit device write commands and rollforward, the signed-manifest-template, and a chain-of-custody checklist.

2) Dual-signature policy: we'll enable the dual-signature requirement for your account and include both primary + quorum keys in the bundle metadata.

3) Dry-run: Jan 5, 2027 at 09:00 CET (we'll reserve 90 minutes). Agenda: 15m intro, 45m guided bootstrap exercise in sealed staging, 20m emergency swap simulation, 10m Q&A. Calendar invite to follow.

4) Ownership and handoff: After the dry-run we'll request a scanned acceptance manifest (signed by your site security lead + site operator). We'll keep an audit copy and mark the bundle as "accepted."

Links: consolidated draft will be uploaded to https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1SealedBootstrapDraft; HubSpot record HS-234981 updated with the plan and dry-run booking.

If there are any last-minute compliance fields your auditor needs, flag them before Dec 22 so we can fold them into the packet.

Best,
